Definition: from G303 and a derivative of the base of G939; to cause to go up, i.e. haul (a net):--draw.
BiblicalUsage: The word is used once, in the parable of the net: when it was full, they drew it to shore, and sat down, and gathered the good into vessels, but cast the bad away. It is the hauling in of the catch — the net full of every kind, dragged up onto the beach for the sorting.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for hauling a net carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the parable's ending — the net is drawn in, the good are kept, and the bad are cast away.
